Home / KEX DNA

Distinct architecture responsibility

Trace the parts behind a composed system.

KEX DNA is kept as a distinct topic in the responsibility map. This brief frames lineage and composition questions for review; it does not assert an implemented KEX DNA interface.

Why this brief is separate

A system’s structural model and the lineage of a particular build are different questions. Treating them separately makes it possible to ask what was composed, from which inputs and under which constraints.

A useful customer question

Can an operator trace a composed result to named inputs, their versions and the contracts preserved between them? A review can identify the records needed to answer that question.

Relevant engineering patterns

The queue’s attributed function contracts, deterministic source manifests and downstream dependency reports demonstrate bounded composition practices. They provide discussion material, not evidence of a deployed KEX DNA product.

Define the contract before claiming the capability

An interface needs an owner, input and output definitions, invariants, failure variations and a verification method. A formal KEX DNA mapping should be confirmed against its authoritative source before integration.

What to bring

Bring an example build or dependency chain whose lineage is hard to explain. The first objective is an inspectable responsibility map and acceptance criteria.
